implementation_notes: Go's idiom is that the standard library has client interfaces you own (`database/sql` is the canonical example and the one Hohpe names as a cheap partial mitigation for databases), so the fix is usually to extend the existing one rather than invent an abstraction. Keep the vendor SDK out of every package except the adapter, and define the interface in the consuming package per Go's accept-interfaces-return-structs convention, so the coupling points at you. Interfaces being implicit in Go cuts both ways here: a small interface makes the seam trivial, and a large one recreated per package becomes its own maintenance problem. `go mod graph` plus `go list -deps` gives the audit.
idiom_name: vendor client imported directly by domain packages
pitfalls: An interface with twenty methods mirroring the SDK's client defeats the purpose; keep it to the operations you use.
`database/sql`'s dialect-neutral API still leaks through in driver-specific SQL, so business rules in SQL remain locked in even with the seam in place.
Struct embedding an SDK client type re-exposes its whole method set to every importer.
